stem: An adult client's serum sodium is 122 mmol/L. How should the nurse interpret this result?

options.D: A mildly high value with no need for follow-up

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists a serum sodium reference interval of 135-145 mmol/L for patients age 1 year and older. A sodium of 122 mmol/L is therefore hyponatremia. Hyponatremia can cause neurologic manifestations because of brain swelling, and clinical severity depends importantly on the rate of sodium decline as well as the absolute concentration.
educational_objective: Recognize a serum sodium of 122 mmol/L as hyponatremia that warrants further assessment, including evaluation for neurologic manifestations and acuity of onset.
source_claim_supported: The reference interval for serum sodium is 135-145 mmol/L for age 1 year and older; hyponatremia can produce neurologic manifestations and severity depends substantially on the rate of change.
correction_summary: Replaced the generic sodium range with a current Mayo laboratory reference interval and removed an automatic provider-notification rule that depends on clinical context and institutional escalation thresholds. Final item tests interpretation plus need for further assessment.
audit_findings: B is the only interpretation consistent with the laboratory reference range. A and D reverse the direction of abnormality; C contradicts the stated interval. No second answer remains.
